## 1) AUB autopilot (module-level) + select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
**What to look for after it finishes**
- A new candidate JSON saved (or champion updated) under `baseline/` depending on how your tool is configured.
- A summary showing whether anything beat `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` on your selection metric(s).
- If it prints “selected best” but no champion file changes, check whether it only writes to a report artifact.

## 2) System autopilot (system candidate sweep)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
**What to look for**
- Any system candidate marked PASS (since you currently have none).
- If results are all FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE, note the top 1–3 by mean and by min (your handoff tracks both).

## 3) Generate the next fix plan
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
This should produce a concrete “what to try next” plan based on recent failures/near-misses.

---

## Quick sanity checks before/after running
- Ensure the champion file exists: `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`
- After each command, capture logs and diff any updated artifacts:
  - `git status`
  - `git diff`
  - confirm new/updated reports under `baseline/reports/`

If you paste the outputs (or the generated `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`), I can help interpret which candidate is actually best and what the next iteration should target (mean vs min tradeoff, lockbox vs tuning regression, etc.).
